common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoIntegration.java:57 - Multiple crypto providers with equal priority are now chosen silently instead of failing.. The check that threw `Multiple crypto providers loaded` is gone. `DefaultCryptoProvider`, `WildFlyElytronProvider` and `FIPS1402Provider` all return `order() == 200`. If two of them end up on the same classpath, the stable sort keeps `ServiceLoader` order, so whichever jar is listed first wins. The only trace is a debug-level log line.

Before this change, a FIPS deployment that also had the default (non-FIPS) BouncyCastle provider on the classpath refused to start. Now it can start quietly with the non-FIPS provider, which defeats the point of FIPS mode.

Fix: drop only the lower-priority providers. If more than one provider ties for the highest `order()`, keep throwing the old `IllegalStateException`.

common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoProvider.java:44 - New abstract `order()` on a public SPI breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations.. `CryptoProvider` is loaded through `ServiceLoader` and can be implemented outside Keycloak. `order()` is added without a default body. Any existing implementation not changed in this PR (custom or third-party providers, test providers in other modules) will stop compiling. If it was compiled against the old interface, it will throw `AbstractMethodError` when `detectProvider` sorts by `CryptoProvider::order`.

I could not check whether other implementations exist in the repository outside the files shown.

Fix: give the method a default, e.g. `default int order() { return 0; }`, or check that every implementation is updated.
